source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 5 (very_hard) activates 6 plates, 11 wires, 6 apertures and 4 anchors per plate, 30° rotation, 2–6 rotation offset steps, five reflection mismatches, 18 px seating tolerance, and 16 px aperture radius.
simplified interaction is explicitly implemented as plate drag plus binder rotate, flip, and explicit seat buttons.
The configured task clock has a 180-second play allowance, a 0 ms observation window, and one frame per observation.
The generator reads the difficulty condition into geometry and tolerance parameters; these are configuration values, not timers or autonomous updates.
Generation uses seeded randomness to create wires, target poses, pins, apertures, and fixed initial poses before the browser starts.
The generated public and hidden states contain the static stage, wires, plates, requirements, target poses, and unique correct wire.
Rotation, flipping, seating, wire selection, and their state changes execute synchronously inside input handlers.
The canvas updates only on pointer and context-menu events; no interval, physics loop, or autonomous task-state update is defined.
The key-miss animation is a transient CSS effect applied after an unsuccessful seat action.
The fresh-failure animation is presentation feedback after a failed submission, not outcome-affecting task evolution.
The grader uses event timestamps only for sequence validity and a broad upper bound; elapsed time does not change the outcome.
Passing depends on completed status, all accepted plate locks, the correct selected wire, and exactly one cut, with no time-dependent criterion.
